blocks.text: The Dow process, perhaps the most famous and industrially important of these, is a multi-step chemical and electrochemical process for extracting magnesium metal from the vast amount of Mg2+ ions in seawater.

items: Seawater is treated with calcium hydroxide (from limestone or oyster shells), precipitating magnesium hydroxide: Mg2+(aq) + 2OH-(aq) -> Mg(OH)2(s).
The magnesium hydroxide is filtered off and reacted with hydrochloric acid: Mg(OH)2(s) + 2HCl(aq) -> MgCl2(aq) + 2H2O(l).
The magnesium chloride solution is concentrated and dried.
Molten MgCl2 is electrolysed in large cells, giving pure magnesium at the cathode and chlorine at the anode: MgCl2(l) -> Mg(l) + Cl2(g).

blocks.text: The process is admired for extracting a valuable metal from an abundant but dilute source on a massive scale, and it changed magnesium production.
